title: Capacity Fit Recommender: right-sizing & autoscale tuning for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Deliver a recommender service and Console surface that suggests optimal committed capacity and autoscaling policy changes for Dedicated GPU pools. The recommender will analyze historical utilization (CPU/GPU, GPU util %, token throughput, queue lengths), workload shape (burstiness, steady-state load), and SLOs (p50/p95 latency, throughput guarantees) to produce:

1) concrete right-sizing suggestions (e.g., reduce commit from 40->32 A100s, or move 3x small hosts into 1x large) with estimated monthly savings and risk delta;
2) autoscaling policy tuning (min/max, scale step sizes, cooldowns, scale-by-throughput vs scale-by-utilization) with simulated headroom curves;
3) a ranked list of low-effort changes (cache config, batching target adjustments, quantization suggestions) that materially improve unit economics before changing commit; and
4) an exportable action plan (CLI or Console button) and canary rollout recipe to apply policy changes safely.

Scope: Dedicated-only (reserved pools). Does not modify runtime or autoscaler automatically in v1 (read-only recommendations + manual approval). Will integrate with Console telemetry and the capacity advisor dashboard.

Key success metrics: adoption by 10 pilot customers, median predicted savings accuracy within ±12% vs post-change billing after 30 days, and no customer-impacting regressions during pilot canaries.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender prototype produces right-size suggestions for target pool and includes expected monthly cost delta in USD and percent
Console view lists top 3 autoscale policy edits with simulated effect on 95th latency and max queue length
Offline simulator can replay 30 days of traces and predict utilization/latency under proposed changes
Canary checklist and runbook documented and linked in ticket
API endpoint for retrieving recommendations (read-only) with auth and rate limits
comments: 2026-02-26 — Kickoff meeting: aligned on inputs (gpu_util, host_count, request_rate, tokens/sec, p95 latency), output format, and risk model. Action: Jun to draft API and Ava to sketch console mockups.
2026-03-02 — Data readiness: telemetry team confirms 90 days of per-pool metrics available in BigQuery. Found gaps for cluster-level preemption logs; follow-up created (ENG-50322).

2026-03-04 — Engineering design review: decided to keep v1 recommender read-only. Trade-offs: faster time-to-pilot vs automation risk. Noted we need a conservative safety margin (default 10%) on recommended downsizes.

2026-03-06 — Prototype run on internal staging pool: recommended cut of 8% commit for steady low-util pool; simulator predicts +5% 95th latency during peak 10-minute windows. Jun: add per-recommendation confidence score.
2026-03-09 — PM feedback (Lina Ortega): surface ROI over 30/60/90 days and label recommendations by risk (low/medium/high). Also require an 'undo' guidance section for each recommendation.
2026-03-10 — Updated: added tie-in to rollout policies (canary size, monitoring checks) and a sample CLI patch command for manual apply. Next: security review if we add automation in v2.
notes: Algorithm plan: (1) compute baseline unit cost = $/token using billing and token counts; (2) build a stochastic workload model from historical per-pool traces (arrival process + sequence length distribution); (3) simulate proposed commit/autoscale configs with our autoscaler model to estimate queueing/latency outcomes; (4) score proposals by expected monthly cost delta and 95% latency impact, and produce a confidence interval derived from trace bootstrap. Start with conservative defaults (min_util_target=0.6, safety_margin=0.10).
